question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Here are 5 ideas that were proposed for this question:

1. Pulse-chase perturbation: does the state outlive the trigger?: Deliver a transient AP-1 stimulus (drug or cytokine pulse, or optogenetic/degron-controlled FOS/JUN induction), withdraw it, and then track AP-1 target accessibility (ATAC-seq) and transcription (RNA FISH, scRNA-seq) over days to weeks. A genuine memory mechanism should show target-state persistence long after AP-1 protein returns to baseline, and the gap between chromatin and transcript decay reveals which layer stores the information.
2. Lineage barcoding to measure heritability across divisions: Barcode cells, let clones expand, then split sister cells and profile them with paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (or MemorySeq-style enrichment for slow-fluctuating genes). Quantifying how much more similar AP-1 motif accessibility and AP-1 target expression are within clones than between them yields a direct estimate of how many generations the state is inherited.
3. Acute AP-1 removal at defined times after state establishment: Use an auxin- or dTAG-inducible degron on c-Jun/c-Fos (or a dominant-negative A-Fos) to strip AP-1 either during state establishment or only after the state is already set, and compare outcomes. If AP-1 is required to write but not to read the memory, late degradation should leave the accessible/primed state and its phenotype largely intact.
4. Re-stimulation kinetics as a functional memory assay: Give cells a first stimulus, allow full recovery, then re-stimulate after varying intervals and measure the speed and amplitude of AP-1 target induction and of the downstream phenotype (e.g., drug tolerance, migration, differentiation competence). Faster or stronger secondary responses that decay with rest interval, and that are abolished by AP-1 loss during the first exposure, are the hallmark of a trained/primed memory.
5. Mapping what physically holds the mark at AP-1 sites: At AP-1-bound enhancers that stay open after the stimulus, profile the candidate storage layers in parallel: histone modifications (H3K4me1/H3K27ac CUT&RUN), nucleosome positioning, DNA methylation, pioneer-factor and BRD4/cohesin occupancy, and enhancer-promoter contacts (Micro-C). Then test causality by targeting erasers or writers (dCas9-LSD1, dCas9-p300) to those specific sites to see which perturbation wipes or installs the memory.

A senior expert reviewing them says they are the ideas everyone in the field would propose first. Propose 5 replacement ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that are substantially less obvious but still concrete, scientifically sound, and feasible for a research lab. Do not repeat or lightly modify the ideas above. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Hysteresis mapping: bistability versus slow relaxation
ideas.description: Titrate a tunable AP-1 input (e.g., degron-stabilized FOS/JUN or a graded cytokine dose) up and then back down along the same concentration ladder, reading a single-cell AP-1 target reporter at steady state at each step, so that the up-ramp and down-ramp branches can be compared directly. A true memory element should show a hysteresis loop with two stable states at the same input level — a signature that a merely slow-decaying state cannot produce — and the loop should collapse if AP-1 self-reinforcement is broken with a TRE-motif decoy sponge or a feedback-dead promoter allele.

ideas.title: Decouple the clock from the cell-division counter
ideas.description: Hold cells at matched post-stimulus times in cycling versus arrested conditions (CDK4/6 inhibitor, contact inhibition, reversible serum withdrawal) and compare decay of AP-1 target accessibility and expression per unit time versus per division, then release arrest to test whether decay resumes on the division schedule. Combine with EdU-pulse sorting and nascent-chromatin readout to measure how accessibility at AP-1 sites is re-established behind the replication fork — whether memory is replication-diluted, replication-refreshed, or indifferent to S phase determines which class of mechanism is even possible.

ideas.title: Dimer-identity relay as the storage variable
ideas.description: Test whether the memory is carried not by AP-1 occupancy but by which family member occupies the site, using ChIP-reChIP or proximity ligation to track the composition shift from labile FOS/JUN to long-lived FRA1/FOSB/JUNB at the same motifs over time, with pulse-SILAC to measure the half-lives of the proteins actually resident at persistent sites. Then swap degrons between family members (chimeras with identical DNA-binding domains but exchanged stability determinants) to ask whether protein lifetime alone, rather than chromatin, sets the duration of the state.

ideas.title: Synthetic sufficiency array: design rules for a memory-competent site
ideas.description: Integrate a combinatorial library of synthetic AP-1 elements at a single genomic landing pad — varying motif number, affinity, spacing/helical phasing, flanking nucleosome-positioning sequence, and co-occurring partner motifs — each linked to a reporter, then pulse the cells and sequence/sort for which configurations retain the on-state after the stimulus is gone. This converts correlative enhancer surveys into a quantitative rule for what makes an AP-1 site remember, and predicts which endogenous sites should be memory-competent.

ideas.title: How many bits, and of what, does the state store?
ideas.description: Stimulate cells with a panel of distinct AP-1-activating inputs at several doses and durations, then at later time points measure single-cell AP-1 target states and compute the mutual information between past stimulus identity/dose and present state. This asks whether AP-1 is a high-capacity memory that preserves stimulus identity or a degenerate one-bit latch, and tracking how capacity decays over time separates loss of amplitude from loss of specificity.
